review_notes: I read all of Dual/Quotient.lean and the definition and simp lemmas in Module/QuotientHom.lean. Those simp lemmas are `quotientHomEquivKer_apply` and `quotientHomEquivKer_symm_apply_mkQ`, and both are `@[simp]` and `rfl`. The three theorems in this file are equalities of linear maps or equivalences. Two of them contain a `LinearEquiv.ofEq` term with an inline proof. None is a good simp lemma: the first two states an equation between composites with `ofEq`/`trans`, which is not a normal form, and the third is the same kind of equation for the inverse. The proofs use `simpa only` with explicit lemma lists, so no unwanted expansion or competing rules show up. Writing the `ofEq` proof twice is a duplication and refactoring issue, not a simp-interface defect, so I did not report it under this rubric. I did not look at Mathlib's simp attributes on the `dualQuotEquivDualAnnihilator` lemmas in detail. I also did not run Lean, so I cannot rule out subtle simp issues in client files.
